In the "research mode" that completely reproduces the actual pachislot "New Pulser", you can freely change the speed of reel rotation, set values, whether or not a flag is established, etc., and you can mark any pattern to make it easier to press. It has a "push marker" function. In "Story Mode" where the story progresses with pachislot, the purpose is to defeat the Pachislot Great Demon King who aims to conquer the pachislot world in a bonus city where people who cannot live without pachislot live.

Game.Name: Pac-Man: Special Color Edition
Game.Overview:
One of the most popular and influential games of the 1980's, Pac-Man stars a little, yellow dot-muncher who works his way around to clear a maze of the various dots and fruit which inhabit the board.
Pac-Man's goal is continually challenged by four ghosts: The shy blue ghost Bashful (Inky), the trailing red ghost Shadow (Blinky), the fast pink ghost Speedy (Pinky), and the forgetful orange ghost Pokey (Clyde). One touch from any of these ghosts means a loss of life for Pac-Man.
Pac-Man can turn the tables on his pursuers by eating of the four Energizers located within the maze. During this time, the ghosts turn blue, and Pac-Man can eat them for bonus points. This only lasts for a limited amount of time, as the ghost's eyes float back to their center box, and regenerate to chase after Pac-Man again.
Survive a few rounds of gameplay, and be treated to humorous intermissions between Pac-Man and the ghosts.

Game.Name: Panel de Pon GB
Game.Overview:
Panel de Pon GB is an unreleased port of Intelligent Systems's flagship puzzle series for GameBoy Color.
A lot of the build got transformed to become Pokemon Puzzle Challenge, but a lot of the original data remains underneath the front-end. A demo can be accessed using a specific set of inputs depending whether you are running this on a GameBoy Color or other prior GameBoy systems.
There has been an ongoing project to restore the game to its original intended presentation.

Game.Name: Paperboy
Game.Overview: In PAPERBOY, all you have to do is deliver the newspaper to your subscribers. While this sounds easy enough, obstacles seem to constantly get into your way...things like dogs, kids on tricycles, traffic, and pedestrians. Since this is your neighborhood, you want punish those who do not subscribe to your paper, so you break their windows with rolled up newspapers. You will even hear the glass shatter thanks to the digitized sound effects and music! At the end of each level there is a bonus course, where you can demonstrate your newspaper-flinging accuracy and earn bonus points. Fortunately, there are three difficulty levels to help you get accustomed to the controls of the game. Will you become the master of your neighborhood or just another punk on a bike? Play PAPERBOY and find out.

Game.Name: Papyrus
Game.Overview: Papyrus is an Action game, developed by Planet Interactive and published by Ubisoft, which was released in Europe in 2000.

Game.Name: Parodius
Game.Overview: A colorized re-release of the Game Boy classic. This Game Boy Color version of the game was originally released as part of the Konami GB Collection Volume 2. Standalone versions exist thanks to the romhacking community.

Game.Name: Parrot
Paws & Perils: Out Of This World
Game.Overview: The world of Terranimalium was a peaceful and diverse world filled with biomes and animals of every kindâ€¦ No wonder the aliens would want to take it- But you and your friends arenâ€™t going to let that happen! Traverse the planet as one of six characters to find a spaceship that can take down the alienâ€™s fleet before itâ€™s too late!

Game.Name: PaZeek
Game.Overview: SkyRank Games scrapped this game and moved on to GBA development, they wrote "The wait is over, PaZeek GBC is NOW available for download. The game is 85% complete with more then 50 playable levels."

Game.Name: Perfect Choro Q
Game.Overview:
While Perfect Choro Q is a racing game, it does not control the same way as most racing games. Perfect Choro Q is turn based racing and controls much like a golf game. The player takes turns with the computer opponents, which starts out with the player choosing which direction the car will go in (which is represented by a dotted line.) Once the desired direction is chosen then the power will be chosen by pressing the A button to stop the moving power meter.
Perfect Choro Q also has some role-playing elements in that the player drives a car along an overworld map and has multiple destinations that can be chosen.

Game.Name: Perfect Dark
Game.Overview:
Joanna Dark has almost finished her training, but she isn't a Carrington Institute agent just yet. She has only one test left - but this time, her mission is for real. In it, she will uncover a far-reaching conspiracy that will introduce her to the shadowy dataDyne Corporation and hint at things to come... From the creators of GoldenEye for the N64 comes Rare's masterpiece... Perfect Dark.
Lots of ways to play! Snipe from long range, commandeer an enemy vehicle - even shoot from a first-person view.
Multiplayer games! Link up and get blown away with eight 2-player games and a total of 35 maps. (Game Link cable sold separately.)
Huge bosses! From helicopters to giant cyborg spiders, go up against some of the most intimidating bosses ever to appear on Game Boy.
Amazing voice and sound! Hear more digitized voices and sound effects in Perfect Dark than in any other handheld game.

Game.Name: Petris
Game.Overview:
Petris - A puzzle game of shapely pets for the Game Boy Color (not compatible with original/pocket)
Build your favorite pets in all shapes and sizes, keep ahead of dropping pieces and make it to the next level!
Game Types Try out a variety game play modes with different incentives and strategies:
Long Pet: Complete progressively longer pets to reach the next level. Tails Cleanup: Clear all tails off the screen per level Crunch-up: Keep ahead as the screen crunches upward and new pets appear Level Up: Classic level-up style Marathon: For the long distance player Head-to-Head 2 Player Two players can compete over Game Boy Link Cable (CGB and GBA) in all game types. * Send crunch-ups to your opponent when you complete long pets or level-up. The last player standing wins the match.
Difficulty Settings A range of difficulty levels make it suitable for all players, from relaxing to hectic: * Easy / Normal / Hard / Expert / Beast
Other Options and features * Choose from multiple sound tracks * High Contrast mode for small and non-backlit screens * Visual hinting for drop location/etc can be turned on/off
Music Credits * KrÃ¼mel (crumb)
Game Copyright Â© 2020 bbbbbr

Game.Name: Phantom Zona
Game.Overview: In Phantom Zona, the player is invited to a school where solving puzzles is the most popular pastime. Upon arriving however, the player will meet Phantom Zona, who reveals that the school is actually a secret base for a gang that fights each other using riddles. When the player enters a battle, he or she is presented with a riddle, and multiple choices answers. Answering correctly will damage the opponent. Answering wrong causes damage to the player. Whoever has the least amount of damage wins. The game makes use of the Game Boy Color's infra-red port. By using anything that emits a infra-red signal, the game generates new puzzles. Players can also use the Game Boy Link cable to swap puzzles.

Game.Name: Pia Carrot e Youkoso!! 2.2
Game.Overview: In the dating simulation Pia Carrot e YÅkoso!!, the player controls Yusuke Kinoshita, a 18-year-old male Japanese high-school student. He intends to have a cool summer vacation, but realizes he has no money. Having no choice, he takes a job in his father's restaurant, "Pia Carrot". Thus begins an adventure much more exciting than the summer vacation he has dreamed about: he gets to know many beautiful girls in the restaurant, and has to decide which one is the love of his life...

Game.Name: Piecrust
Game.Overview:
Piecrust is a logic puzzle game for the Game Boy Color based on Nanogram / Picross.
Each row and column in a grid has a series of numbers. These refer to number of adjacent squares that should be filled. Each block of solid squares are separated by one or more unfilled squares. Blocks of solid squares can start anywhere in a row or column.

Game.Name: Pilgrim's Peril
Game.Overview: Roguelike dungeon-crawler game for the Game Boy.

Game.Name: Pine Creek
Game.Overview:
The disappearance of a young girl in the previously quiet small town of Pine Creek raises the popular belief that a cult is behind the crime and many other ritual killings before her.
Her best friend will do his best to solve why, how, and who is behind it.
PINE CREEK is an adventure game focused on exploration, story, and following clues. Have friends, think about life, think about death, eat tasty food, and play games in the arcade!
The project started out as a Game Boy game before being colorized in late 2020 and brought to the Game Boy Color platform. The Game Boy Color version remains completely backwards compatible with the original Game Boy.

Game.Name: Pitfall: Beyond the Jungle
Game.Overview:
Swing into non-stop action with Pitfall Harry Jr. on Game Boy Color!
Plunge into a magical rift within the steaming jungles of South America to enter a new dimension filled with treachery. Guide young Pitfall Harry Jr. as he swings, leaps and combats deadly creatures to protect the Moku people from evil Scourge.
- 15 treacherous levels filled with traps and treasure. - Wield your trusty pick axe and swing across gaping chasms on a vine. - Magmoids, Demon Bats and Fire Djinns are only the beginning of the horrible monsters awaiting you. - Devious traps like vanishing floors, moving platforms and bubbling lava line your path to glory.

Game.Name: Planet of the Apes
Game.Overview: Released in conjunction with the 2001 cinematic remake, PLANET OF THE APES, the game actually takes its plot from the 1968 original film. Play as Ulysses (the character that Charlton Heston originated), a human who has fallen to a post-apocalyptic Earth ruled by primates. Ulysses quickly discovers that he is being considered a sort of messiah by many of the apes (he's considered an enemy by others), and it is becoming readily apparent that the creatures want him to save them from the dangers of this new world. The game is packed with puzzles to solve, and the graphics are among the best ever created for the Game Boy Color. Modes of play include: Normal, in which Ulysses walks from location to location; Athletic, in which the hero runs and jumps through each level of the story; and Stealth, which requires Ulysses to crawl and slink into hidden areas not accessible in other modes. It's not easy to compare PLANET OF THE APES to any other video game, and that's really its charm.

Game.Name: Player Manager 2001
Game.Overview: Player Manager 2001 is the Game Boy Color version of the long running football management series that started on the Amiga in 1989. It follows the norm of the genre and lets you take control of any team in the top two divisions of five European countries (England, France, Germany, Spain and Italy). As the manager it is your task to buy and sell players, lay up training schedules, set contracts and scout for new players. Most importantly, your job is to choose the right squad, and create tactics that takes advantage of your opponents' weaknesses. There are different staff modes meaning that you can choose to put some parts of the game as auto. The matches are text based.

Game.Name: Pocket Billiard Funk: The 9 Ball
Game.Overview: An adult game, billiards arranged in a cute pop. In addition to full-scale billiards, it is equipped with the original game system "Tamappy" that takes advantage of the characteristics of Game Boy. In billiards called club nine-ball, you can usually enjoy 9 balls, but there is also a tamappy mode where you can play games using spirits hidden in billiards called tamappies and items called tamappies. While honing your billiard skills, you can collect and exchange tamappies and tamappies.

Game.Name: Pocket Bomberman
Game.Overview:
Long, long ago, the sun was covered by a dark and heavy cloud. It was said this cloud was caused by a monster that had sealed the Sword of the Sun. Legends also says that to break the seal, a hero must collect five Power Stones that are guarded by monsters. Bomberman takes up the challenge as he is the last hero strong enough to defeat such monsters.
This is a side-scrolling platform game. In each world, you must clear four areas by killing any monsters within. To kill a monster, you drop a bomb. After a few seconds, the bomb explodes in a four-way blast. If the monster is within range of the blast, it is killed. After you clear these four areas, you must clear a fifth area by killing a boss to clear the world and collect its Power Stone.
Be careful, though, because if Bomberman is touched by a monster, touches a dangerous item or is caught in the blast of his own bomb, you lose a life. After all lives are gone, you get the option to restart that last area or quit. In most areas, you can, though the placement of bombs, find items to increase your jumping, speed, blast radius, etc.

Game.Name: Pocket Bowling
Game.Overview: The action and excitement of using a big ball to knock down white pins comes to the Game Boy Color with POCKET BOWLING. Make your selection from six different bowlers, including an android. Once you have a bowler that matches your style of play, use the Training mode to work on picking up spares and to get the hang of the game controls. When you are ready for some action, play against a human or computer opponent in the Standard mode. If you want an extra challenge, try to win a tournament against four opponents in four different alleys. In all of the modes, getting the perfect shot requires lining it up, setting the proper amount of spin and power, and letting the ball go at the right time. Play POCKET BOWLING, and become master of the lanes.

Game.Name: Pocket Color Billiards
Game.Overview: Pocket Color Billiard is a Sports game, published by Bottom Up, which was released in Japan in 1999.

Game.Name: Pocket Color Mahjong
Game.Overview: A four-player mahjong that you can hit with a unique character. You can choose a member from 12 people, such as cheap, full-fledged professionals, and screaming. Communication battles are possible using a communication cable. You can enjoy full-scale mahjong with an advanced thinking circuit.

Game.Name: Pocket Color Trump
Game.Overview: Realistic play with communication cable settings. You can enjoy 5 types of games: "Millionaire", "Speed", "Page One", "Dobon", and "Blackjack".

Game.Name: Pocket Cooking
Game.Overview: A cooking simulation game where you practice cooking with your helper "Food Angel". The purpose is to make the restaurant prosper, aiming to be a true chef in order to revive the leaning restaurant. Select ingredients from the storage location and reproduce the actual work such as cutting, simmering, stir-frying, and seasoning in the game to complete the dish. Set the menu considering the price of food, the number of dishes, etc., and open the shop. If the customer's reaction is bad, the store's reputation will decline, the number of customers will decrease, and events such as eating away will occur. Occupations are Japanese, Western, Chinese, and ethnic. Cultivation of ingredients in the garden at home and cooking confrontation with rivals. You can exchange original dishes with your friends using the communication cable.

Game.Name: Pocket Densha 2
Game.Overview: This time, with the cooperation of Odakyu Electric Railway and Nankai Electric Railway, Odakyu Romance Car, Nankai Rapi: t, etc. will appear. Beginner's subway mode, and after clearing, new routes will appear and there will be plenty of content! The expression of landscapes and curves that could not be expressed in the previous work, the coloring of trains, etc. have been greatly enhanced. You can enjoy the scenery of Odawara Castle, Hakone Mountain, Kansai Airport, and Koyasan. The site view is also powered up. In addition to the stations, you can enjoy tunnels, railway bridges, and elevated tracks from the site view.

Game.Name: Pocket Family GB2
Game.Overview: The second family development simulation in which the player takes care of the family who moved in as a landlord. This time, the number of owners has increased from one to four, and it has become possible to visit the house with a lopo. You can get items in the mini game "Walking in the back mountains", and you can enjoy various things such as equipping the lopo parts with lopo parts and planting flower seeds in the flowerbed. Five types of mini-games that improve the abilities of the family and four types of care games that improve the intimacy with the family have been created. The number of characters appearing this time has increased to about 300 types for album creation. Take care of many characters and fill the album.

Game.Name: Pocket GI Stable
Game.Overview: A horse racing game that anyone can play, whether it's a horse racing freak or a horse racing beginner. There are three ways to play: training mode, training mode, and original stakes. In the training mode, you will train a racehorse as a trainer and compete with a little less than 10,000 rival horses that have entered the race based on the Central Horse Racing, aiming to win the Derby Horse, Triple Crown Horse, and All G1. In the breeding mode, a racehorse that you want to make is involved from the seeding stage, and a type of game that raises electronic pets such as taking care of a mother horse, giving birth, taking care of a foal, and training to become a racehorse. In the original stakes mode, you can register the horses you raised and race them, or you can enjoy the race with your friends using a communication cable or password.

Game.Name: Pocket Hanafuda
Game.Overview: Perform a "Hanafuda game" with 12 unique characters. The Hanafuda game is played by selecting two types of games, "Flower Matching" and "Koi-Koi". The player plays 12 games with each character, and the one with the most wins advances to the next. And if you win all the characters, it will be the ending! !! Of course, it is also possible to play "Flower Matching" and "Koi-Koi" alone.

Game.Name: Pocket King
Game.Overview: A fantasy simulation game that inherits the pedigree of the masterpiece "King of Kings". There are plenty of original elements such as more than 150 types of units and characters such as humans, fairies, and dragons, 179 types of special skills, "class change" items and "party formation" that strengthen the units! You can also exchange units with friends using a communication cable, and you can enjoy the collection to complete the unit picture book. Not only those who are addicted to "King of Kings" but also those who are new to the series can enjoy it widely.

Game.Name: Pocket Lure Boy
Game.Overview: The goal is for the player to become a boy who loves fishing, acquire lures and fishing techniques while competing with rivals in various places, and finally win the "legendary fisherman" in the fishing game. You can create a "fish picture book" by releasing the fish you caught during the adventure to your own lake. There are 60 kinds of fish that appear in the game! Collecting all of these is also one of the players' goals. Also, if you use a communication cable, you can play fishing games and exchange lures and fish with your friends.

Game.Name: Pocket Monsters Go! Go!
Game.Overview:
Monster Go! Go! Go!! is a hack of The Smurfs 3 released in the late 1990s for the Game Boy Color. The Smurfs 3 was originally in monochrome, but was colorized in this hack - it was later re-released officially in color as The Smurfs Nightmare, and a subsequent version of the hack was based on this release.
Almost all the graphics from the original game are replaced, and so does the intro and ending text. Bizarrely, the intro text appears to be replaced with a poorly translated version of My Heart Will Go On by CÃ©line Dion. Aside from the title screen, the game's use of color is limited, which gives it the appearance of a Super Game Boy game. The game suffers from extreme slowdown, running consistently at about half speed, possibly due to the colorization process.

Game.Name: Pocket Music
Game.Overview: Make music on the move with Pocket Music, the music creation game. Create your own music from a selection of samples, drum beats, baselines, melodies, and other musical instruments. Play them back, save them to your cartridge, or swap them with a friend. Features include more than 600 different high quality samples and instruments, custom drumbeats, baselines, melodies and sound effects, a riff editor to allow you to create your own sounds, and prearranged tracks to demonstrate the capabilities of the game.

Game.Name: Pocket no Naka no Oukoku
Game.Overview:
Pocket no Naka no Oukoku (ãƒã‚±ãƒƒãƒˆã®ä¸­ã®çŽ‹å›½, Kingdom in Your Pocket) is a hybrid adventure/simulation game by Hect, best known as the developers of Moon Crystal. It's also possibly the most obscure commercially developed Game Boy game in existence.
The leaked game identifies itself internally as version 0.950, built on March 7th, 2001, and I would estimate that it's 75-80% done; it can be played from start to finish, but the last few areas are obviously incomplete and it has several glaring bugs.

Game.Name: Pocket of Horror
Game.Overview: What if WORLD OF HORROR was released on the Game Boy Color? Four MYSTERIES, and the old LIGHTHOUSE Many PALETTES to choose from CHARACTERS with different stats A rough approximation of combat, events, items, etc

Game.Name: Pocket Pro Wrestling: Perfect Wrestler
Game.Overview: A versatile handheld wrestling game, with over 20 different moves and a 3D enviroment to utilize every corner and sides of the ring. A roster of 12 wrestlers go against each other for the championship.

Game.Name: Pocket Pro Yakyuu
Game.Overview: The game development just like an actual professional baseball game is reproduced on the screen. In one-player play, you can play pennant races or play against computers. Communication battle is possible with two people. Pennant race can be selected up to 135 games. You can play up to 4-7 games in the Japan Series. Both professional baseball Central League players are officially recognized by the Nippon Professional Baseball Organization and appear with their real names and data. Infrared input from remote control signals of household appliances changes the player's parameters. There are 45 registered players per team (30 fielders, 15 pitchers). Foreign player participation rules, etc. also comply with the "official baseball rules". The edit function also supports sudden trades and the addition of foreign players. Fictitious trades and dream team creation are also possible by changing the player name.

Game.Name: Pocket Puyo Puyo~n
Game.Overview: This time Puyo talks! Introduced the long-awaited "chain voice" to GB. The voices of "Ei!", "Fire!", And "Ice Storm!", Which are familiar at the event, will make the battle even more exciting. Equipped with "official battle mode". Bet a sign with your name on it and fight in online battles. If you win the online match, the rank of "Puyo class" will rise and the official handicap will be calculated automatically. With this, even beginners who can not make chains and advanced players who can make big chains can experience a close battle.

Game.Name: Pocket Puyo Puyo Sun
Game.Overview:
Puyo Puyo Sun is the third entry in the main Puyo Puyo series of real-time puzzle games, its title being a pun involving the Japanese word for "three". The evil Dark Prince has caused the sun to augment its size and power to dangerous levels, and thus the Puyo Puyo world is on the verge of being scorched unless you prevent it.
The game features three distinct story campaigns, each pitting you against a different set of enemies which you must battle in classic Puyo Puyo fashion: In each stage you face off against an opponent in two different play areas, one for you and one for your opponent. As the blob-like "puyos" start falling in your play area, you must align them and create groups of the same color in order to clear the screen before you get flooded with puyos. Chaining puyos of different colors allows you to send several "garbage" puyos to the opposing player's play area in hopes of either flooding it, or slowing his advance, and whoever defeats the opposing player moves on to the next challenger.
New for Puyo Puyo Sun are the Sun Puyos, which can be added to combos for extra damage. Also includes 2P vs gameplay, challenge modes and galleries and other bonus features.

Game.Name: Pocket Racing
Game.Overview: Pocket Racing is a racing game, which was released in Japan in 1999.

Game.Name: Pocket Smash Out
Game.Overview: Pocket Smash Out is based on the classic multi-level arcade / puzzle game â€˜BREAKOUTâ€™ with the various levels all themed with exciting Manga graphics. The levels become progressively harder as you work your way through all of the 16+ levels. There are over 90 different brick layout patterns in the Championship and with the harder levels being kept till last there is more than enough challenge for even the most experienced player. The object of the game is to â€˜fireâ€™ your ball at the bricks and catch it on the rebound (watch out for those bonus balls !!) and progress to the next level.

Game.Name: Pocket Smash Out & Race Time
Game.Overview: "Pocket Smash Out" and "Race Time" are two separate game titles that were released together as a "Mega Value Double Pack" for the Game Boy Color. The release date for this compilation was February 23, 2001. "Pocket Smash Out" is a Breakout-style game with manga-themed graphics and challenging levels, while "Race Time" is likely a racing game.

Game.Name: Pocket Soccer
Game.Overview: It's time to show your soccer skills! Pocket Soccer brings the world's most popular sport direct to the palm of your hand. Create your own team from more than 200 players or choose from 32 ready made teams, then work your way up the league in this fast paced game! Play head-to-head with a friend using the Universal Game Link cable (sold separately) or trade players in order to make your team the very best!

Game.Name: PocketWare
Game.Overview: PocketWare is a microgame collection for the Game Boy Color in the vein of WarioWare. A submission for the GBCompo25.

Game.Name: P.O.D.: Proof of Destruction
Game.Overview:
This is a homebrewed game, run on Gameboy Color.
Original version by Shaun Southern - Mastertronic Limited. Commodore 16/Plus4, 1986. Created with GB-Studio 2.0.0 beta5!
Original Story:
P.O.D has no pretentious storyline and no mega-reality to justify its existence. It is simply an exciting addictive shoot-em-up! There are 9 difficult levels to survive, each more difficult than the last and all superbly balanced for playability and action. You play across an interconnecting grid of wire, along which your P.O.D (what else?) may be moved. The aliens arrive (usually) from the top and descend repidly in orderly fashion, intent on causing P.O.D actual physical pain. You can't move over the damage until it heals (A few second), but the Bad Guys can move! Each level is timed (20 sec) as shown on the screen and to win through all you have to do is stay in one piece. Should you succeed a bonus extra life (every second level + 1 life - max. no.3) You will need them all!
In the unlikely event of your achieving a good score, the high score table records the event (only 1 hi-score, the best of all time) and save it to the memory.
Firing will often be a problem because if the machine overheats, you can't shoot!
Keep moving and keep firing.
Developed by RajcsÃ¡nyi LÃ¡szlÃ³ and published on his itch.io page on January 6, 2022.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Adventure
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Adventure is a bootleg platformer released for Game Boy Color in 2000 by Makon Soft. This game turns out to be a hack of Sonic Adventure 7, which possibly makes it the first game to hack an existing hack, Sonic Adventure 7 being a hack of Sonic 3D Blast 5 on the Game Boy.
The intro in the game features screenshots of specific PokÃ©mon entries from PokÃ©mon Gold's Japanese PokÃ©dex, complete with the actual Japanese descriptions for each. The borders change with each entry as each screen is a four-color BG image instead of being comprised of various sprites and BGs like in the official PokÃ©dex from PokÃ©mon Gold, PokÃ©mon Silver and PokÃ©mon Crystal.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Ambrosia
Game.Overview:
Ambrosia is a hack of PokÃ©mon Crystal with a bespoke PokÃ©dex of 253 popular PokÃ©mon with new and powerful abilities. The game has an updated story, a tailored set of modern mechanics and items, significant QoL features, an extensive post game, and detailed documentation. It has been described by players as a "power hack" meaning the player has access to many powerful tools and so do enemies. The game has some mechanics typically found in difficulty hacks, such as level caps, but the game, while challenging, is not intended as a difficulty hack. For example gym leaders don't have full teams until the 7th gym, gym leader aces are slightly below the level cap until mid game, and mandatory enemies almost never have access to something the player doesn't have access to. The player also has access to in-battle data, letting them see the enemies stats, ability, moves and item, in addition to field effects on both sides.
Fundamentally Ambrosia is a game focused on fun and power progression. I hope the passion and enthusiasm that went into making it comes through in the gameplay more now than ever before.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Anniversary Crystal
Game.Overview:
The second fully-custom game mod, this time for PokÃ©mon Crystal. Anniversary Crystal adds more content than ever before while blowing the existing mod, Anniversary Red, completely out of the water. New dungeons, new encounters, new maps, music, trainers, and more! Take a journey from your hometown in Kanto like never before on your quest to capture all 251 Pokemon!
Features: - New story (Start from Pallet Town in Kanto!) - Tougher Challenges - Trainer customization (Change your trainer color!) - New maps - New encounters - Fairy type - New plot twists

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Black and White 3 Genesis
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Black and White 3: Genesis is intended as a further sequel to Black 2/White 2 Versions. It takes place in Unova, around 5 years following the events of B2/W2. In this game, you play as a young trainer from Humilau City and will embark on a journey around the region to catch PokÃ©mon, collect Gym badges, and thwart the plans of a mysterious group claiming to be Team Plasma, a terror group that was supposedly disbanded years ago.
Features: - Fully demade Unova region on GBC hardware - New original story featuring many characters from B/W/B2/W2 - Demade music tracks for Unova locations - New Cries for all Gen3+ Pokemon - 255 moves from throughout the first 5 generations - Physical/Special split on moves - Fairy type added, and type chart adjusted to account for it - Many various items from newer games - Running Shoes available from the start - Reusable TMs - Move Reminder - Much more Bag space - All evolutions available in a single player game - Reusable Repels - Various other minor quality of life improvements - 252 Pokemon available, selected from throughout the first 5 generations of Pokemon

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Blue Version Full Color Hack
Game.Overview:
This is a colorization hack of Pokemon Blue, done entirely using ASM. It takes full advantage of Gameboy Color hardware, which is much more capable than the Super Gameboy. The overworld is fully and properly colorized, and with colorized attack sprites, even battles are more colorful!
In addition to color, Pokemon and Trainer sprites have been imported from Pokemon Gold/Silver/Crystal, and so has the battle HUD. If you donâ€™t want this, the â€œvanillaâ€ patch does not touch these.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Bronze 2 Version
Game.Overview: In PokÃ©mon Bronze 2 you start as either a boy or a girl trainer in Old Oak Town with the goal of collecting all 8 badges and then defeating the Elite Four. But along the way, an evil team is trying to execute their plan to steal, kidnap and make money. It even includes a full second region with post game!

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Bronze Version
Game.Overview: A Pokemon Gold ROM hack inspired by the likes of PokÃ©mon Brown and PokÃ©mon Prism. Is basically your generic PokÃ©mon affair, It is set right after the events in Gold and you leave home and get a PokÃ©mon from a professor and defeat gym leaders and the elite four with a group of antagonists to battle along the way, and a rival.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Card GB2: GR-dan Sanjou!
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Card GB2: Great Rocket-Dan Sanjo!, released March 28, 2001, is the Japanese-exclusive sequel to the original PokÃ©mon Trading Card Game, also for the Game Boy Color. Like its predecessor, the game was developed by Hudson Soft and published by Nintendo, and was first announced in January 2001 by Japanese website WatchImpress. It includes new enhancements, such as the ability to choose the gender of the player character, a training mode to help new players, a Deck Diagnosis to rate the effectiveness of a player's deck, and a new group of antagonists known as Team Great Rocket. The game features all cards from the original game, along with new cards from the fourth set, Team Rocket, as well as cards originally exclusive to Japanese vending machines and the PokÃ©mon Trading Card Game Instructional Video Intro Pack, bringing the total number of cards to 445.
Like the previous title, players must travel across the game world challenging non-player characters to simulated battles using rules adopted from the original tabletop version. All locations from the original are present, along with a new setting known as GR Island which contains its own Battle Masters for players to encounter. Though an English release in North America was deemed "likely" by website IGN in 2001, the game has not been made available outside Japan. PokÃ©mon Card GB2 earned a 29 out of 40 score from Japanese Weekly Famitsu magazine.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Christmas
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Christmas (originally called PokÃ©mon Skeetendo Christmas Hack) is a hack game based on PokÃ©mon Gold. It was done by the user Mateo of PokÃ©community and Skeetendo, Inc.
Instead of being a completely new game, like other hacks intend to be, Christmas serves more as an upgrade of PokÃ©mon Gold, in the same vein as the Pokemon Generation's third version. The game follows pretty much the same over-all plot of PokÃ©mon Gold and other main-franchise games, but the events occur and are focused around Christmas time. Other changes: Â· Flash not required for any caves Â· Coin case is in B1F Goldenrod Dept Store -- used to purchase tutor moves Â· Berry trees give 24 Â· Jasmine has a female Steelix Â· Weekday events happen every day Â· Whirlpool not needed in Dragon's Den Â· Pokeflute not needed to wake Munchlax Â· Bill's house now gives you vitamins if you show the right pokemon Â· The Super Rod is in Blackthorn Â· All flee mons now only rarely flee instead of sometimes flee: magnemite, grimer, eevee, porygon, dratini, unown, snubbull, phanpy, teddiursa, delibird, cubone. Â· Secret boss in the Viridian basement Â· Easter egg â€“ how did the moon ball work in the original game?

Game.Name: Pokemon Crooked Crystal
Game.Overview:
Pokemon Crooked Crystal is a reimagining of the classic Pokemon Crystal, designed to enhance gameplay while preserving its nostalgic charm. For example, HM03 Surf is now a Key Itemâ€”the Lapras Suitâ€”though a reusable TM for Surf remains available at the same time.
The story takes an intriguing turn: After losing a rigged bet on the Bug Catching Contest, Professor Elm mired in debt, refuses to pay Team Rocket. Tasked with raising a PokÃ©mon to protect Elm, youâ€™ll travel through Johto, earning Gym Badges, exposing Team Rocketâ€™s corruption, and unraveling their deeper, more sinister plans.
This hack introduces a more diverse set of wild and trainer PokÃ©mon, an expanded and intensified Team Rocket/Radio Tower plotline, added lore about Kantoâ€™s limited map, and plenty more surprises in this more challenging version of Crystal.

Game.Overview:

Changes:

An expanded Kanto, with restored dungeons, more trainers, and more items. More sensible PokÃ©mon distribution, and more generous HM compatibility. Every PokÃ©mon available on one save file, and all room decorations can be bought or are gifted to you. Fixed off-model PokÃ©mon sprites. Palettes were also improved for a good amount of PokÃ©mon. Some QOL features, like â€œRunning Shoesâ€ (works by holding down B), and an automatic Repel reuse message. Fixed bugs and glitches. The Celebi event, now restored! To get it, simply head to Goldenrodâ€™s PokÃ©mon Center after beating the League.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Clear
Game.Overview: Crystal Clear is an expansive, open-world Gen II ROM hack developed by ShockSlayer. It features no new moves, stat changes, or PokÃ©mon species, just Gen II as youâ€™ve always known it, but experienced in a way you never have before. Collect all 16 badges, catch all 251 PokÃ©mon, challenge the new Elite Four, re-challenge gyms, explore new locations, and uncover fresh story arcs in familiar regions. Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Inheritance
Game.Overview:
Crystal Inheritance is a time-traveling adventure through Johto! In a twist on the classic Pokemon experience, instead of collecting badges to become champion, you unite Johto against a dark force threatening its future.
Use your knowledge of the world to craft pokÃ©balls from new apricorns, discover Hisuian and Ancestor forms of Johto PokÃ©mon, and explore Johto like never before.

Nothing is inevitable - what path will you choose?

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Kaizo
Game.Overview:
This is a significantly more challenging hack of Pokemon Crystal, where you can obtain all 251 Pokemon in Second Generation.
Numerous areas have been redesigned, many dungeons and routes are more treacherous than before. Every non-boss trainer in the game has an AI boost, and the default movesets are made to be far more threatening. Team Rocket members and especially Team Rocket leaders are a considerable threat.
Wild Pokemon distribution is vastly improved, with levels fairly close to trainers. You can catch quite a variety of pokemon early on. In addition, the odd egg from the daycare man can yield one shiny pokemon, which could be either one of the starters, Dratini, Larvitar, one of two Tyrogues with different attack DVs, Magby, Smoochum, Elekid, or an Eevee.
Apart from Slowking, who evolves by water stone, you can evolve trade evolutions by level up. Eevee evolves into Espeon and Umbreon using Sun Stones and Moon Stones respectively. You can purchase stones as early as goldenrod, where the game will start to pick up on the difficulty.
Every major Boss in the game has shiny pokemon, and apart from the early rival fights, every boss in the game has a full team of six, with dangerous movepools, healing items, and as time goes on, held items. Initially the Gym Leaders will stick to their specialty types, but as soon as you get to the Rival in Ecruteak, they will start to use diverse pokemon with a few of these specialty types, using moves corresponding to that type as coverage or status, and sometimes, counters. These major bosses include Team Rocket Executives, the Elite Four, and Champions.
After seven badges, you will face against very powerful enemies with fully evolved and dangerous pokemon, and you will eventually reach level 100 after the eight badge. The Rival at the end of Victory Road may catch you off guard, and the Elite Four and Champion will probably be the most difficult part of the game.
Post-game will be slightly less intense than victory road, apart from Kanto Gym leaders, who will be on part with the Champion in terms of difficulty. However, there are 4 superbosses, including Leader Blue, who will be far more difficult than the others. The other three include the Trainer House, Red on Mt. Silver, and one obscure Rival fight at the indigo plateau, that only appears on Mondays and Wednesdays only after you beat him in Mt. Moon.
A major update involves Revives, Max Revives, and Revival Herbs; they cannot be used during battle. They can only be used outside of it, so there are consequences to losing your pokemon in battle, in which you cannot revive them while you are battling, only when it is over.
Added the Team Rocket Battle Music to Executives and Scientists. As well as ethers in shops, some graphic changes, and bicycling in Goldenrod Underground and Team Rocket Hideout.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Leaf

Mainly what this hack does is add in a follower mechanic, similar to Yellow or HeartGold/SoulSilver. The difference is that, instead of having your Pokemon follow you, it's another player.
Features
Play as Red and Leaf - Hold B and press Select to switch between them - Use two different teams! - Battle and trade with eachother All Pokemon are available without trading with another game Instant text speed option Feraligatr can learn Waterfall

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Legacy
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Crystal Legacy is an enhancement hack that aims to improve Generation 2â€™s most underdeveloped areas, whiling holding on to the mechanics and feel that made it unique. Rather than bring modern PokÃ©mon design philosophy to Crystal, Legacy only makes changes based off precedents set in the gameâ€™s original design. This ensures an authentic gen 2 experience, while bringing the game to itâ€™s full potential.
Features Include
Dynamic Gym Leader level scaling for â€˜non linearâ€™ part of Johto. The teamâ€™s and levels of Chuck, Pryce and Jasmine scale to whether you have 5, 6, or 7 badges. Gym Leader teams optimized. Leaders see more Gen 2 representation, while still retaining their original aces (e.g. Bugsy keeps his Scyther, but Metapod and Kakuna are replaced with Pineco and Ledian). Movepools see increasing diversity and complexity. Gym Leaders use held items. Improved level curve. Gym leaders and trainers no longer fall off in the late mid-game, only to spike in the Elite Fuur. The game now sees a more linear rise in leveling, with expanding trainer teams to provide more EXP. Players who donâ€™t grind will still be under leveled to the champion, but this is intentional and typical for most PokÃ©mon games. PokÃ©mon availability increased. Kanto locked Gen 2 mons like Houndour added to Johto. Route encounters have been diversified. Gen 1 trade mons evolve by level up. Gen 2 trade items now simply work like evolution stones. Increased accessibility to evo items. Fossils + GS Ball added to Ruins of Alph. All legendaries are now catchable. Gameplay Balancing. Dark-type is now Physical while Ghost is Special. DRASTIC improvements to PokÃ©mon movepools. Balancing to actual moves (notably large improvements to bug and fighting type). Weak single evo mons + other underperformers have seen some stat buffs (i.e Misdrievus is now closer stat wise to Mismagius, but not on par). Item Improvements. Flower shop now sells Berries. Cianwood pharmacy sells Stones & Ethers. Post radio tower Mahogany mart sells Upgrade and Metal Coat. Mahogany, Blackthorn, and Celadon now sell TMs. X Items cannot be purchased. Storyline enhancements. Slight adjustments to timing of Silverâ€™s character arc. A man helps Lance uncover the Rocket Hideout. Team Rocket has seen Executives named as Archer and Ariana. â€˜Hyuck-Hyuckâ€™ Rocket now has a small character arc. The game now has an explanation for the missing Legendaries of Kanto. Quality of Life: Unique PokÃ©mon Sprites, Running Shoes, Bigger Bag, Early EXP Share, Delete HMs whenever, TM pickup now says move name, PC added to Elmâ€™s Lab and House after Tohjo Falls, Gameplay Icon that shows Weather, Bugs Fixed, Brick Piece (found in Goldenrod Warehouse) now evolves Hitmontop, Odd Egg always has good DVs, Happiness System makes Friendship Evos faster, Third Trainer Card show Kanto Badges, bugs fixed AND MORE. Rematch Johto Gym Leaders after becoming Johto Champion. Kanto is now itâ€™s own separate league. Gym leader teams have competitively set teams of 6. Upon beating them, you must rematch the Elite Four for title of Kanto Champion before facing Red. Consider this section a â€˜challengeâ€™ post game. Fight the creator (Smith), production manager (Craig) and video editor (Weebra) in the Trainer House.
What Stays the Same
No Physical/Special split All PokÃ©mon keep their typing No new PokÃ©mon added No new trainers added Badge boost remains Trainer AI is untouched TMs are single use (all TMs eventually become available for purchase) Most original wild encounters remain where they were, outside of some overly redundant ones All storyline outcomes are the same, although some get to their conclusion slightly differently

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Ultimate

PokÃ©mon Crystal Ultimate is a ROM hack aiming to remaster the original PokÃ©mon Crystal with improved playability, balance, and challenge while preserving the original story and PokÃ©mon. The hack revises moves, typings, learnsets, base stats, and PokÃ©mon availability, making nearly all PokÃ©mon viable and the game suitable for Nuzlocke challenges. A Classic mode preserves a more traditional experience by removing most stat and type changes. Features: - Complete remaster of PokÃ©mon Crystal with improved balance and playability - Overhauled moves, typings, learnsets, and base stats - Increased game difficulty with redesigned level curve, custom moves, DVs, and trainer stats - Expanded PokÃ©mon availability on trainer teams - Nuzlocke-compatible difficulty - Expanded locations with extra trainers and items (Ilex Forest, Ice Path, Victory Road, Kanto) - PokÃ©mon type changes, palette swaps, and type matchup rebalancing - Classic mode preserving traditional stats, types, palettes, and lower shiny rate - All 251 PokÃ©mon obtainable through normal gameplay - All Johto PokÃ©mon obtainable before the League (except specific legendaries/starters) - Quality-of-life improvements (music, sprite work, gameplay enhancements) New gameplay features and battle system enhancements

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Version

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal Version: Emu Edition

It does this through combining all wild encounters from the three gen 2 games, making starters available in some areas, the Celebi event restored, and a partial restoration of the Safari Zone to help fill out the PokÃ©dex.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Crystal World
Game.Overview: PokÃ©mon Crystal World is a hack that has some unique elements compared to the original game. Instead of having to battle Elite Four after gaining 8 gym badges, you'll be traveling to Kanto instead to collect another 8. After doing all that, you may go to Mt. Silver to battle Red. Game.Name: PokÃ©mon: Cubic Crystal
Game.Overview:
POKEMON: CUBIC CRYSTAL is a remix of Crystal thatâ€™s recognizable but distinct, a sort of â€œwhat if Crystalâ€™s story was as different from Gold/Silver as future same-gen sequels?â€ approach.
POKEMON FEATURES:
- Fully revamped stats, with BSTs given a general baseline of 400 for weakmons, 450 for mid-tier early mons, 500 for most mons, and slightly higher for starters and such. - Tweaked typings for many and vastly improved learnsets for all! - All evolutions available without trade, - All evolution items available before Elite Four, including a stone shop in Cianwood. - Evolution levels tweaked for many mons with high requirements. - Improved level curve for wild Pokemon, particularly in Kanto.
MOVE FEATURES:
- Dark is physical and Ghost and Poison are special to reflect the nature of their moves (of all three types, only Lick and Poison Sting are now in the â€œwrongâ€ category as of Gen IV). - Overhaul of dozens of moves, including an accuracy buff to virtually every move with 70 BP or less. - Iron Head and Ominous Wind added to increase move options for Steel and Ghost, respectively. - Field moves such as HMs can be used by any mon that learns them as long as the physical TM/HM is in your possession - All TMs can be repurchased, with new TM shops appearing as the game progresses. - Move Reminder in Violet City teaches old moves for a modest fee. - Bill replaces Move Tutor outside of Game Corner and teaches Thunderbolt/Ice Beam/Flamethrower. He appears after Radio Tower rather than after Elite Four, and is no longer limited by day.
TRAINER FEATURES: - Overhaul of virtually every trainer to provide a better level curve (not Kaizo difficulty, but in keeping with a full two-area game). - Improved Rival that steals both unchosen starters, because why would he not do this? - Improved Gym Leader rosters, with later leaders gaining Pokemon out of their selected type to counter said typeâ€™s weaknesses. - Pryce now acts as the fourth gym, with Chuck/Jasmine/Morty acting as interchangeable 5/6/7; while their teams are not dynamic, the game nudges towards this order. - Rematches available for all Gym Leaders, with Johto Leaders giving bonus optional rematches before the Elite Four.
OTHRT FEATURES:
- Deeper integration of Gym Leaders and Elite Four members outside of their gyms a la Platinum to create a sense of place in the world and offering small story beats in Kanto. - Suicune and Ruins of Alph quests are incorporated more deeply into the plot, with Karen replacing Eusine as our resident legendary hunter. - Press B to run! - Repel and Escape Rope are now reusable key items given early in your quest. - Pocket PC allows for PC access on the fly. - As Whirlpool as a move is deleted, there are no more pointless Whirlpools in the game.

Welcome to the world of Suden! It's year 1571, and it's been around a thousand years since the great war, The Crisis, ended. One thing leads to another, and eventually, the main character and his classmate end up journeying to the Rocky Mountain in order to help the university do research on the Elemental Orbs. Little did they know, their simple task was yet to become an epic, and hazardous adventure..
PokÃ©mon Dark Energy is an RPG game that is implemented as a Rom Hack on top of Pokemon Silver.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Diamond
Game.Overview:
The game follows a protagonist traveling through various regions capturing and battling creatures called â€œPokÃ©monâ€ (actually Telefang monsters with altered sprites and names). The narrative is loosely structured around defeating a series of opponents and advancing through dungeons, often with contrived story elements added by the bootleggers. Traditional PokÃ©mon elements like Gym Leaders and the Elite Four are mostly absent; progression relies on battling wild creatures and a few scripted trainers. Dialogue is often broken English or mistranslated.
PokÃ©mon Diamond and Jade are bootlegged versions of Keitai Denjuu Telefang 1. The Power Version was used to make Diamond, and the Speed Version became Jade. PokÃ©mon Jade has also been used for the name for an edited version of a pirated game called Sonic Adventures 7.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Fool's Gold
Game.Overview: In Pokemon Fools Gold, all of the PokÃ©mon have been reworkedâ€¦ think Alolan/Galarian forms, for all the Pokemon. All 251 PokÃ©mon are available in-game without trading. All of the trainers and wild encounters have been reworked to fit as well. In addition, there have been a few visual tweaks, and a few new places to explore, too!

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Gauntlet Gold
Game.Overview:
How hard can you make a vanilla Pokemon game? Trashlockes are usually the answer to that question, keeping vanilla enemies unchanged while forcing the player to use low-tier encounters.
But what if you want to raise difficulty without changing trainers OR wild Pokemon availability? Gauntlet Gold is an experiment with that idea. It is vanilla Pokemon Gold, but with difficulty upped by forcing long trainer gauntlets with limited access to healing items.
Every route, cave and gym will trap you in until you have cleared every trainer. You can no longer buy potions from marts; what you find on the ground is all you get for healing within gauntlets. Even Indigo Plateau will not sell healing items, so you will want to manage your resources carefully to be able to beat the Elite Four.
Basically, this game is inspired by the resource-management strategies of the ironmon challenge, as well as the gauntlet system used in Garbage Green. Although Gauntlet Gold is easier by design, as it doesn't also impose a trashlocke. It makes for a fun and fast-paced challenge run.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon: Jade Version

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Kalos Crystal
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Kalos Crystal is a sequel to Unova Red. This is a re-imagining of Generation 2, where the first generation of PokÃ©mon was the Unova PokÃ©dex, and the new second-generation PokÃ©mon is the Kalos PokÃ©dex. This game features all Pokemon from generations 5 and 6, and like in Unova Red, all Pokemon in the Pokedex is obtainable within a single playthrough.
Aside from the new PokÃ©mon, the game functions primarily the same as the original. The biggest difference is the inclusion of Fairy types. This game also adjusts the type matchup chart to the modern chart first used in Gen 6. All new attacks added into Unova Red are still here, as well as several new attacks to fill out the new Fairy type, as well as add some signature moves to Gen 6 PokÃ©mon, and simply flesh out some underrepresented types. An equivalent number of moves were removed from the game as well, mostly signature moves of Gen 1 & 2 PokÃ©mon, or simply moves that did not fit well with the Gen 5 & 6 PokÃ©mon.
Like in Unova Red, all standard trade evolutions have been changed to standard level-up evolutions, and some of the stone evolutions were modified as well. All Gen 5 PokÃ©mon evolve identically to how they did in Unova Red. A full list of evolution methods can be found in the spoiler logs.
Some TMs have been altered, and a full list can be found in the spoiler logs. Notably, like in Gen 2, TMs are still only for one-time use. Also, like in Gen 2, moves are still classified as Physical or Special based on type. The only exception (as in Unova Red) is that Ghost is classified as SPECIAL, while Dark is classified as PHYSICAL. Also, the new Fairy type is classified as SPECIAL.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Lavender

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Lunatic Crystal
Game.Overview:
Pokemon Lunatic Crystal is a difficulty ROM Hack that provides not only a major challenge, but is also an attempt at making Gen 2 more balanced and enjoyable, while also retaining the charm of the original games.
Lunatic Crystal has the following features:
â€¢ Trainer parties have been massively improved. Every trainer has a more varied and stronger line-up and all of the important opponents have custom movesets (many of which also use Hidden Power with an advantageous type), held items, better Pokemon and are at a higher level.
â€¢ Lunatic Crystal has Level Caps that set you on equal terms with the bosses that are increased with each badge/met condition. At a certain level your Pokemon will no longer gain EXP, no matter what you do whether be it battling, using Rare Candies or using the Daycare. As an extra feature Pokemon also no longer gain EXP once they reach Level 100.
â€¢ Lunatic Crystal features a brand new secondary Rival in Lyra, who will obtain the starter weak to the player's and challenge the player at various points in the main story, both in Johto and Kanto for a total of 7 battles. Silver also has an extra battle in Johto.
â€¢ Stat EXP and all of the badge boosts have been removed. The 25% Status miss chance that the AI had is also gone. This makes fights more challenging and sets the player on equal footing with enemy trainers. Furthermore Vitamins (with the exception of PP UP) and X items have been removed.
â€¢ Lunatic Crystal removes the "SWITCH" battle mode, every single trainer battle is on "SET" mode and the player is prohibited from using items in battle against important opponents.
â€¢ The progression of the game has been made more linear, rather than open like the original Crystal to better help with the level curve. There are also changes to the Gym Leader order, Eusine's Cianwood City battle (and the Suicune event), as well as the Tin Tower section is now enforced. The game also features extra mandatory opponents. The Sprout Tower is also a mandatory location when the player visits Violet City for the first time and acts as the first, real challenge of the game as well as a check that prevents progression. Some Gym Leaders will also refuse to accept your challenge if you do not have the right amount of badges.
â€¢ The player can now catch all 251 Pokemon. Every single legendary can be caught as an overworld encounter, with the exception of Raikou and Entei who are still roaming Pokemon.
â€¢ Improved level-up learnsets: the vast majority of Pokemon now have much better learnsets, with all moves being learned at lower levels. All evolution stages share the levels at which they learn moves, so the player no longer needs to delay evolutions and can enjoy a power boost right away. This does not apply to most stone evolutions (the exception being for example Eevee), however.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Picross
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Picross (Japanese: ãƒã‚±ãƒ¢ãƒ³ãƒ”ã‚¯ãƒ­ã‚¹ PokÃ©mon Picross), not to be confused with the 3DS game with the same name, was a Game Boy Color game slated for release in 1999, with snapshots of the game published in several video game magazines, but was ultimately scrapped.
A near-final prototype dump of the game was surfaced online on September 10, 2020, as part of a major leak of Game Boy / Game Boy Color prototypes, which was dubbed "Nintendo Gigaleak 3" by the fans.
The game's UI is seemingly based on Picross 2, as the games have similarities such as map-based level select screen and multi-piece puzzles. As a Gen I spinoff game, the game features sprites of all 150 PokÃ©mon available in PokÃ©mon Red/Green/Blue. The game was planned to be compatible with Game Boy Printer, with the sprites being printable by being viewed on the in-game PokÃ©dex.
The game is divided into 11 levels, each one featuring 15 puzzles (with the final one being locked). Once 8 puzzles are completed (halfway the level), the 15th puzzle would be unlocked. A perfect completion of each puzzle occurs by solving the puzzle within the time limit determined to it, with a Master Ball as the reward; otherwise, a normal PokÃ© Ball would be awarded.
There is a variety of themes (music / border) assigned to certain PokÃ©mon, which appears as Ash's partner in the level select map. The only one available from the start is Pikachu, and more could be unlocked by completing odd-numbered levels, accompanied by a "catching" animation sequence.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Pikachu Edition

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Pinball
Game.Overview:
There are two tables in the game, red and blue. Each table has its own details and gameplay elements.
Each table has different "locations" that you play, which determine which PokÃ©mon are available for capture. A subset of available locations are displayed slot-machine style in the beginning of a game, and pressing A will select your starting location and launch the first ball into play. After that, each table has its own mechanism for advancing to the next location, including the locations not available at the start of the game.
"Catch Mode", when activated, starts a 2 minute window of opportunity where you can attempt to capture a PokÃ©mon. Once you activate "Catch Mode", you must hit the pop bumpers 6 times. Each hit unlocks 1/6 of an image of the PokÃ©mon currently up for capture. Once the image is complete, the PokÃ©mon appears on the table, where it must be hit 4 times with the ball to capture it.
"Evolution Mode", when activated, starts a 2 minute window of opportunity where you select a captured PokÃ©mon (from the current game in progress only) and attempt to evolve it into another form. This is the only way to add the evolved form to your PokÃ©dex. Once you select a PokÃ©mon, you must hit targets on the playfield. There are up to 6 targets, but only 3 of them have items in them you need to evolve a PokÃ©mon. The others create a time-wasting sequence before you can hit targets again. If you hit a target with an item, the item appears on the playfield and must be collected with the ball. Once you've collected 3 items, the hole in the center of the board opens up. Sinking the ball in the hole successfully evolves the PokÃ©mon.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Pink

Game.Overview: This hack of PokÃ©mon Crystal Version by Rangi is a comprehensive overhaul that modernizes the Gen II experience with extensive additions, improvements, and quality-of-life updates. All 253 available PokÃ©mon (including evolutions from later gens like Gliscor, Sylveon, and Mamoswine) can be caught in a single playthrough, with sensible placements and updated evolution methods. Many moves from future generations have been added, others removed, and learnsets align closely with Gen VI. Battle mechanics incorporate the Physical/Special split, Fairy type, updated stats and type chart, Gen V's money loss formula, and refined shiny odds. Quality-of-life changes include Running Shoes, reusable TMs, faster egg hatching, infinite bag space, level 1 egg hatches, smoother catching mechanics, and an optional Nuzlocke mode with dupes and shiny clauses. New and restored locations expand Johto and Kanto, while added events, trades, Wonder Trades, and legendary respawns enrich the world. Trainers feature new classes, rivals (like Lyra), rematches, and better AI, with difficulty gradually increasing to a final boss at level 100. TMs, HMs, items, PokÃ© Balls, and fossils have been updated, with buffs to moves, types, and many PokÃ©mon stats. Faithful and expanded versions are available for purists or those who enjoy balance tweaks. Graphics and sound are enhanced with improved sprites, devamped music, unique mini-sprites, and visual polish, while numerous text and naming updates reflect modern terminology. With thoughtful bug fixes and hidden surprises, this hack offers a refined, content-rich Gen II adventure for both nostalgic fans and challenge-seekers alike.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Ruby
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Ruby (å£è¢‹æ€ªç¸ è–è®ŠçŸ³ in Chinese regions, å¯µç‰©å°ç²¾éˆ çµæ™¶å¡”ä¹‹çŽ‹ in Taiwanese regions) also known as Pocket Monster Ruby and PokÃ©mon Pikecho, is a bootleg game for the Game Boy Color likely released around 2002, possibly 2003. Its title is taken from the then-recent Game Boy Advance game of the same name.
The game puts you in control of Ash Ketchum (Satoshi) (though not explicitly stated as being him) and has you traveling to each town and defeating its leader, much like in the traditional PokÃ©mon games. Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Salt Crystal Version

PP is fully restored at the end of a battle. - Poison: in addition to damage, drains a tiny amount of PP every turn. - Sleep: lasts between 2 and 3 turns; taking damage wakes the sleeping PokÃ©mon sooner; restores PP every turn. - Freeze: lasts between 2 and 3 turns; taking damage thaws the frozen PokÃ©mon sooner; grants a boost to the defenses of the frozen PokÃ©mon (similar to Reflect and Light Screen); ends under harsh sunlight. - Flinching: can carry over to the next turn, meaning that PokÃ©mon going second can also flinch the opponent. - Obedience rules apply equally to all PokÃ©mon, traded or otherwise.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Silver Version

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Soul Crystal

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Super Gold 97
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Gold and Silver came out in 1999. Over 20 years later, people are still playing these games. Be it on traditional Gameboy devices or through emulation. Why not look at PokÃ©mon Super Gold 97, a ROM hack using Gold as its base? The 97 on the name is unclear, but regardless, this ROM hack stands out on its own.
This ROM hack is based on Gold, and many of the story elements are the same as Gold and Silver. You are a new trainer who sets out on a journey to help Professor Oak with researching PokÃ©mon, very much like the very first games. This story is built on the foundation that was pulled from the demo itself, and has you traverse Nihon, based on the entirety of Japan, while you collect badges and catch PokÃ©mon. You'll also have to face off against Team Rocket, who are building a machine that would give them incredible power over PokÃ©mon! Silver is portrayed in the manner that he was in the demo - not as an antagonist, but as an energetic rival, kind of similar to gen 4's Barry. The story is admittedly kind of simple, but intentionally so. It was written to feel like the story that might have been in the demo had it been completed.
Features - Current Version is v7.41 - Game is fully feature complete, may have minor bug fix updates in the future - Graphics fully pulled from the Spaceworld demo, complete with Pokemon sprites, overworld tilesets, trainer sprites, etc, along with a handful of sprites I had to redesign myself to better match the art style of the demo - Interface elements such as Pokedex, status screen, etc have been redesigned to appear similar to the demo - Pikachu minigame! (press Left +B on title screen and wait for music to end) - 251 Pokemon, the complete Pokedex as it appeared in the demo. The main way that this differs from what would have been in an "official" game is that all 251 Pokemon are obtainable in one save file - New key items that match the story presented in the game - Evolutionary stones that match the Demo (Heart Stone, Poison Stone) as well as an additional Covenant Orb that allows for the evolution of Pokemon that would normally require trading - New in-game status booster held items, pulled from the demo - 8 badges, Pokemon League, a full length game - A new original postgame map not present in the Spaceworld demo - Type chart inspired by the demo - Full support for the original Game Boy - Full support for the Super Game Boy - Full support for the Game Boy Color (with two different color modes) - Improved level curve compared to final Gold and levels are generally higher, leading to a slightly tougher game but still not overly difficult - Additional rematches for Gym Leaders and Pokemon League - Skateboard! - Additional moves based on scrapped moves from the demo - Several Beta music tracks - Expanded bedroom decoration system
If you want information on the finer details of the game, such as movesets, base stats, encounter locations, etc, join the Discord for Super Gold 97 where you can download the Player's Guidebook that contains all this information and more!

PokÃ©mon TCG Generations is a Rom Hack that replaces all the PokÃ©mon in the game with some PokÃ©mon from each of the Generations (1-9), changing Attacks, Resistance and Poke-powers. And just like the originals, the Sprites are Directly based on Cards from the TCG, so you may recognize some =D.
Features:
* There are a total of 310 cards on the Rom, 82 more than in the Original Game. * At the start of the game you can choose whether to play as Mark or Mint, exactly like in the Sequel! and you can even start with 7 different decks instead of just 3. * All PokÃ©mon Cards have been replaced by PokÃ©mon from other Generations, with Some Exceptions (Eevee, Ditto, Horsea, to name a few, this is due to effects of the Cards or are related to PokÃ©mon introduced after those.) * The Meta, I have dedicated a lot of time to developing the Meta of this game, mainly I have worried that each card has something that makes it interesting to use. In general most Basic Pokemon are not as strong as in the original game and there is a focus on using Stage 1/2 Pokemon. * All the PokÃ©mon Sprites were Replaced with Sprites made by me, Obviously Following the "Style" of the game and now using up to 3 palette per sprite just like the sequel!. * The vast majority of attacks in the game have been changed in some way or another, including new attacks with new effects. * Each Booster Pack will now give 11 cards total. * The Sprites of the Main Duelists of the Game have been replaced by those of the Sequel (Because they basically look better), and Now each of the Club Masters will give you an extra Booster Pack (Basically they give you 3 in total) * Almost all the Cards in the Game can be obtained through the 4 booster packs and there is even a clear way to know which Booster each card is in and now who were the artist of the original cards and sets!

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon TCG Neo
Game.Overview:
A new player character and new player character portraits! Balance changes! Booster pack edits! Typo fixes! Animation fixes! Fight Ronald more! Basically, everything and the kitchen sink was added to the game, thereâ€™s probably even a pokÃ©mon from Orre in there for all I know!
This hack, PokÃ©mon TCG Neo, is a near complete overhaul of the base game in terms of battling. Why? Because all the generation 1 cards in this game have been replaced with generation 2 cards, and everything has been balanced.
Featuring your favorites from Neo Genesis all the way to Skyridge, so many cards have been added and replaced that it 's completely changed the way this game is played. PokÃ©mon, attacks, abilities, even a few trainer cards- altered to create a completely new battling experience.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Trading Card Game
Game.Overview:
The greatest PokÃ©mon Trading Card Game players of all time - the Grand Masters - are looking for one player worthy of inheriting the four rare, Legendary PokÃ©mon Cards! Build new decks with the Auto Deck Machine, hone your skills on the Challenge Machine and test your ability in Challenge Hall. Expand your card collection, duel your way through 8 Club Masters and earn the right to challenge the Grand Masters in the PokÃ©mon Dome! Shadowy figures, wise instructors and powerful opponents await in the ultimate trading card game adventure.
* Includes over 200 of your favorite PokÃ©mon Trading Cards, plus new cards exclusive to the Game Boy game! * Learn how to play the card game, build and manage decks and duel with other card players in step-by-step tutorials. * Duel a friend using a Game LinkÂ® cable (sold separately) or generate new cards using the Infra-red Card Pop feature. (Available with Game Boy Color only) * Basic reading skills are needed to fully enjoy the story.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Ultimate End
Game.Overview:
PokÃ©mon Ultimate End is a good Pokemon Crystal Hack. It is not for those who like nice graphics because it uses PokÃ©mon Crystal Codebase with GBC graphics. But it is really for those who want a quality game to play with harder mode and new features.
This hack is a lot more difficult than PokÃ©mon Gold/Silver/Crystal you have played and after you meet Lance GYM Leader, your rivals own Level 100 PokÃ©mon and so hard to beat them. Good Luck!!!
Not like the original version, you live Ice Cave which is next to New Bark Town (instead of New Bark Town). You start to do your dream to beat the strong PokÃ©mon Trainers, GYM Leaders and Elite Four.
Along your way, you have chances to meet a lot of strong trainers with high level PokÃ©mon. So you must prepare your team carefully with suitable PokÃ©mon to enter battles.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Wasteland
Game.Overview:
Embark for a short, yet challenging PokÃ©mon adventure!
Discover Dakos, a small region set in a hostile wasteland, with a unique story. Goals
Dakos is a small region with only 3 towns, all accessible from the beginning.
Iâ€™ve created an exciting hack offering players a short, immersive adventure. With this game, you can start and finish in a single run but expect a challenging and captivating experience. The storyline is coherent, and much effort has gone into the dialogue to keep players engaged.
Itâ€™s highly recommended that players engage with non-playable characters (NPCs) to understand their surroundings and progress through the adventure. However, players who prefer to grind can also do so.
The wasteland theme of the game is evident in the storyline and tile set, with trainers and the wilderness being particularly hostile, especially at night. Furthermore, items are scarce in Dakos so players wonâ€™t find any potions in this ROM.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon Yellow Chaos
Game.Overview: PokÃ©mon Yellow Chaos is a fan game developed and published by DaTateYT. The game was made to test out rom hacking tools, but then later became a full game. There is a second game in development as of right now. The second game is a ROM hack of PokÃ©mon Emerald and will be called PokÃ©mon Chaos 2.

Game.Name: PokÃ©mon: Yellow Legacy
Game.Overview: The Yellow Legacy project is the prequel to Crystal Legacy by content creator Patrick Smith (TheSmithPlays), and the second project in his planned Legacy series. It is based on the PokÃ©mon Yellow Disassembly. The Legacy project is focused on changing the base game in a way that adds quality of life additions and better balancing with the benefit of twenty years of hindsight. The primary goal of each mod is to keep the original feeling of the game while still making meaningful improvements for the player. This means that certain idiosyncrasies of the first generation of PokÃ©mon games will remain, as they are considered an essential aspect to the core experience.

Game.Name: Pokettohiro!
Game.Overview: A group of brave heroes must gather the fragments of the Magic Crystal to face the evil Black Knight and thus prevent the destruction of the kingdom. But it will not be an easy task, for this they will have to overcome countless obstacles, defeat huge monsters and visit all kinds of places. Will these little heroes be able to restore peace to the kingdom?

Game.Name: Pokimals! - A Roguelite Adventure
Game.Overview:
Deal with the strange and insane inhabitants of The Island as you explore a series of ruins that were discovered beneath the surface.
It's your 13th birthday, so the government says you're old enough to die in a hole! (It's all in the name of adventure, so it's cool.)
Pick from one of 13 starters and make your way into the depths of The Ruins. Defeat 5 critters and the door will open, and the ruins may give up some of their loot. Do you use it to boost your team or sell it for supplies? As you defeat your instructors at The Site, you'll unlock more ANIMALs in The Ruins as well as more resources for your excursions!
Use a clean, Version 1.1 Pokemon Crystal ROM for patching.
Features: - 251 ANIMALs (Fakemon based on real world things) with brand new pics and Dex entries - A completely original soundtrack - Randomized dungeon runs so that you'll never have the same trip twice - Leaders (Teachers) can be fought in any order and scale accordingly (but you have to pay a scaling fee; Education ain't free, you know!) - Teachers can now have any ANIMALs from their type specialty - Character pics with their dialogue like most modern 2D RPGs - A goofy, sarcastic tone to everything (I'm sorry if you're not a fan.) - Appearances by various celebrities, including beloved President, Abraham Lincoln! - A real, working cigarette item! (Your animals will look so cool!) - Redone UNOWNs as actual letters - A third gender option (Dinosaur, the third gender is dinosaur)

Game.Name: Polaris SnoCross
Game.Overview: Get on a snowmobile and drive your way to victory with POLARIS SNOCROSS. Try to master 10 different courses that take you through ovals, twisting bobsled runs, and several treks through the wilderness. When you are ready for some competition, try to win the Tournament Cups, where you will have to take first place from two other racers. After winning, you will be able to upgrade your vehicle before moving on to the next race. With three different Cups to win, there is plenty of racing action. If you get tired of racing computer-controlled opponents, hook up a link cable to challenge your friends to a race. You will become the greatest snowmobiler of all time in POLARIS SNOCROSS.

Game.Name: Pong: The Next Level
Game.Overview: PONG is the original videogame and PONG: The Next Level brings all of the action of the classic to the Game Boy Color. The game is an electronic version of table tennis (or Ping Pong, if you prefer). Players move a paddle up and down, trying to hit the ball past their opponent, and the first player to get 11 points wins. In addition to the classic Pong, there are three other tables to play on. On the Glacier level, two penguins waddle around between the paddles and affect the trajectory of the ball when it hits them. In the Soccer level, players must maneuver two paddles to try to put the ball into the opponent's net. Finally, the Jungle stage has two rollers in the middle that can change the ball's trajectory. Get all of the action of the first major videogame with PONG: The Next Level.

Game.Name: Pooh and Tigger's Hunny Safari
Game.Overview: A.A. Milne's beloved characters come to interactive life in this wonderful expedition through the Hundred Acre Wood. In order to ensure their party will be, Pooh and Tigger are going to need some honey (known in Milne's world as "hunny"). In fact, the duo will need to find dozens of pots full of the stuff, and that will mean searching the entire forest. Much to Pooh and Tigger's collective dismay, the area is populated by dozens of insects, angry animals, and environmental dangers. In addition to searching for the hunny, you'll have to help your pals find such popular characters as Rabbit, Piglet, and Owl, as well as unlocking dozens of hidden areas and special power-ups. Three mini-games Veggy Match, River Run, and Fence Off can also be uncovered, and you can save all of your progress and resume play with a password. The game spans 18 levels and five diverse environments including The Spring Glade, The Nighttime Forest, Autumn Heights, Creepy Caves, and Winter Wood.

Game.Name: Pop'n Music GB
Game.Overview:
pop'n music GB is a scaled-down version of Konami's long-running pop'n music franchise. Notes scroll toward the bottom of the screen, and the player must tap the correct buttons in time with the music to play along. Play well, and the "groove meter" increases, but play poorly and it will drop. If the groove meter is high enough at the end of the song, the player can move on to the next song.
The 9 buttons of the original game have been reduced to 5 for the Game Boy's control setup, and there are 25 tracks included; 15 arranged tracks from the first three arcade and console releases, along with 10 new original tracks. The game includes a single-player Original mode, as well as a 2-player Versus mode.

Game.Name: Pop'n Music GB Animation Melody
Game.Overview: This is a scaled-down port of pop'n music: Animation Melody using the 5-button setup of pop'n music GB. It includes chip arrangements of 20 anime theme songs, and also offers the same Original and Versus modes that the previous GB release offered.

Game.Name: Pop'n Music GB: Disney Tunes
Game.Overview: This is a scaled-down port of pop'n music: Disney Tunes using the 5-button setup of pop'n music GB. It includes a slightly different selection of Disney music compared to the console release, arranged for the Game Boy's sound chip, and also offers the same Original and Versus modes that the previous GB releases offered.

Game.Name: Pop n' Pop
